resumen: When focus moves and where the camera looks.

bloques.alt: Two drawings of focusing. On the left, single focus: a still subject with a focus square that stays fixed on it: 1, single, locks focus. On the right, continuous focus: a subject moving from left to right, with the focus square following it: 2, continuous, follows the subject.
bloques.pie: 1 Single: focus locks on a still subject. 2 Continuous: focus follows a moving subject.

bloques.texto: To focus well, decide two things: when the camera focuses (the mode) and where it looks (the area).

items: Single ([[enfoque-simple|AF-S, One Shot]]): when you half-press the shutter button, focus locks and stays put. It is for still subjects: landscapes, objects, posed portraits. You can reframe without losing it.

Continuous ([[enfoque-continuo|AF-C, AI Servo]]): while you hold the shutter button half-pressed, the camera keeps focusing. It is for moving subjects: sports, kids, wildlife. If you lock it and recompose, it may focus on something else.
Automatic (AF-A, AI Focus): it chooses between the two by itself, but it is less predictable. Better to choose yourself.
One point: you choose where. It is the most precise, for portraits or objects.
Zone or group: a cluster of points, for a subject that moves around a predictable place.
Wide or automatic: the camera picks the points, and you don't know which ones it will pick.
Tracking: you pick a subject and the camera follows it across the frame. It works with birds or with kids.

bloques.texto: Many cameras recognize faces and eyes, and some also animals, birds and vehicles. Turning it on helps most in portraits and with wildlife.
Some cameras have a back button (AF-ON) that focuses without using the shutter button. That way you focus with your thumb and the shutter button only takes the photo.
Tapping the screen focuses at that point: see “Tap to focus and expose”.
Set single focus and take a photo of someone standing still. Then set continuous and photograph someone walking toward you. Check which one comes out sharp.
